channel.title: Business Insider Africa - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Business Insider Africa (africa.businessinsider.com)

item.title: Ethiopia secures $400 million UK investment to expand power grid linked to GERD dam
item.description: UK government-backed investor Gridworks has signed agreements to develop and finance around $400 million in electricity transmission projects in Ethiopia, as the country steps up efforts to upgrade its power grid and draw private investment into its energy infrastructure.

item.title: Top 10 African countries with the strongest naval fleet in 2026
item.description: Africa's coastlines serve as economic frontiers rather than merely geographical borders. The security, competitiveness, and prosperity of African economies are oftentimes determined by events at sea. In this atmosphere, the strength of a country’s naval fleet has become a practical requirement rather than a symbolic show of force.

item.title: Singapore‑based energy firm unlocks 950m oil reservoir in West Africa’s Sèmè field well
item.description: A major offshore discovery by a Singaporean energy firm at West Africa’s Sèmè field is reshaping expectations for the basin, after tests confirmed a 950-million-barrel oil reservoir that could transform the economics of a field long considered marginal.

item.title: South Africa’s rand still undervalued after strong rally, survey finds
item.description: Despite its recent bullish run, South Africa’s rand remains undervalued at current levels, according to a survey of investors and economists.

item.title: Africa’s top gold producer offers levy cut to smooth path for higher gold royalties
item.description: Ghana’s finance minister has offered to cut a mining levy by two percentage points in a bid to win industry backing for a proposed gold royalty overhaul that mining companies say could discourage investment.

item.title: US says some military forces have been deployed to Nigeria
item.description: The U.S. has deployed a small team of troops to Nigeria, marking the first public acknowledgement of American forces on the ground since Washington carried out airstrikes on Christmas Day.

item.title: Muammar Gaddafi’s son, Saif al-Islam reportedly assassinated in Libya
item.description: Saif al-Islam Gaddafi, the son of Libya’s former leader Muammar Gaddafi and once considered his political heir, has reportedly been killed, according to statements cited by Libyan media on Tuesday, February 3, 2026.

item.title: African Energy Bank rolls out $10bn first phase funding for Nigeria, 2 other countries
item.description: Africa’s oil and gas sector is poised for a fresh wave of investment following the launch of the African Energy Bank, which will mobilise an initial $10 billion to finance priority energy projects across the continent, beginning with Nigeria, Angola, and Libya.

item.title: Trump signs last-minute US–Africa trade preference extension to preserve duty-free African exports
item.description: U.S. President Donald Trump has signed into law a one-year extension of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), temporarily restoring preferential access for eligible African exports to the American market and averting what many governments feared would become a prolonged disruption to trade flows and jobs across the continent.

item.title: The Epstein files reach Africa: How Congo’s oil funds almost ended up in Epstein's hands
item.description: The case of office misconduct involving the United Kingdom's former Labour minister and US ambassador, Peter Mandelson, has extended its reach to Africa, specifically the Republic of Congo.
